hero.title: Welcome to
hero.imageAlt: Welcome photo of Les Jardins de Wesserling
hero.firstParagraph: Since 2000, the Les Jardins de Wesserling association has been working to transform the Parc de Wesserling into a vibrant, creative and community-focused place in the heart of the Vosges Mountains.
hero.secondParagraph: Through the kitchen gardens, events and educational spaces, the association promotes and enhances this heritage site while supporting social and professional inclusion and strengthening local solidarity.
hero.thirdParagraph: Today, around twenty people taking part in work integration programmes, supported by a dedicated team and many volunteers, contribute each year to the life and development of the gardens.
hero.fourthParagraph: Above all, Les Jardins de Wesserling is a place of sharing, creativity and learning, open to anyone who wishes to get involved or simply discover the site.
hero.fifthParagraph: A warm welcome to everyone who would like to join us.
hero.sixthParagraph: On behalf of the Board of Directors

garden.intro: The Wesserling kitchen garden introduces visitors to environmentally friendly gardening while offering a unique and relaxing stroll.

centralPath.imageAlt: Photo of the kitchen garden at Les Jardins de Wesserling
centralPath.description: The central pathway linking the former ponds forms the backbone of the kitchen garden. It creates a connection between horticulture and Wesserling’s industrial heritage. The arrangement of vegetables, flowers and herbs recreates textile patterns once designed in the former factory. Each year, a new composition is presented in connection with the theme of the Festival of Mixed Gardens.

pedagogy.imageAlt: Photo of the educational garden at Les Jardins de Wesserling
pedagogy.description: On either side of this axis extend the four sections of the educational kitchen garden. Their plots demonstrate gardening methods that work alongside natural processes: crop rotation, beneficial plant associations, the use of helpful insects and wildlife, soil and water management, and more. A pathway through a hedge reveals habitats for beneficial species useful to gardeners. Educational panels and games introduce visitors to the secrets of gardening.

orchard.imageAlt: Photo of the orchard at Les Jardins de Wesserling
orchard.description: A heritage quince orchard, a terrace of berries and aromatic plants complete this abundant garden, whose produce is sold or transformed at the Resto du Potager.

accessibility.imageAlt: Photo of a resting area at Les Jardins de Wesserling
accessibility.description: To ensure accessibility for everyone, including people with reduced mobility, numerous resting areas immersed in the vegetation are located throughout the kitchen garden pathways.

garden.membership: By becoming a member of the association or making a donation, you benefit from a 66% tax reduction, as the association is recognised as serving the public interest. Your support helps fund employment initiatives.

meta.title: The Kitchen Garden Restaurant — Les Jardins de Wesserling
meta.description: Discover the Kitchen Garden Restaurant, a light and seasonal restaurant located in the heart of Les Jardins de Wesserling.

atmosphere.imageAlt: Photo of the Kitchen Garden Restaurant at Les Jardins de Wesserling
atmosphere.firstParagraph: The Kitchen Garden Restaurant offers an original setting surrounded by flowers, vegetables and aromatic plants, within a décor inspired by fabrics inherited from the former Wesserling Textile Printing Factory. It is a social restaurant where service is provided by people taking part in work integration programmes.

solidarity.imageAlt: Photo of the social restaurant at Les Jardins de Wesserling
solidarity.firstParagraph: Having lunch at the Kitchen Garden Restaurant means supporting people seeking employment, as well as farmers from the surrounding mountain area, since part of the restaurant’s produce comes from their farms. More broadly, it also contributes to promoting Wesserling’s remarkable industrial heritage.

menu.imageAlt: Photo of the menu at the Kitchen Garden Restaurant
menu.firstParagraph: The menus reflect all the flavours of the kitchen garden: assorted fresh vegetable platters, vegetable tarts, seasonal fruit melba desserts, soups, syrups, and more. These are complemented by products from nearby mountain farms, including charcuterie and cheese platters.

produce.imageAlt: Photo of the fresh produce at the Kitchen Garden Restaurant
produce.firstParagraph: The vegetables, berries and herbs grown in the gardens are sold fresh at the Kitchen Garden Restaurant or transformed into jams.

meta.title: Festive Events — Les Jardins de Wesserling
meta.description: Discover the festive events organised by Les Jardins de Wesserling: the Festival of Mixed Gardens, the Nature Festival, and much more.

festive.title: Festive Events
festive.intro: Numerous festive events bring Wesserling’s industrial heritage to life throughout the year (link to the Parc website). Refreshments and light catering are provided by the work integration programme of the Les Jardins de Wesserling association: tarte flambée, plain or gratinated pretzels, sweet crêpes (and ice creams depending on the season), drinks including garden syrups. The Les Jardins de Wesserling association organises three events: the Garden Swap, the Music Festival and Cocktail Evenings. The association also provides light catering during events organised within the Parc de Wesserling, such as Pâques en Folie, Heritage Day, the Barefoot Trail Festival, the Night-Time Fairies, the Autumn Festival and Christmas in the Garden.

easter.imageAlt: Pâques en Folie at Les Jardins de Wesserling
easter.title: Pâques en Folie
easter.subtitle: During the week around Easter. From 12pm to 5pm. In the courtyard of the Wesserling Farm. Paid entry.
easter.firstParagraph: Egg hunt. Fun and creative workshops.
easter.secondParagraph: Refreshments, tarte flambée, plain or gratinated pretzels, crêpes, Easter Bunny afternoon treats.
easter.thirdParagraph: Thousands of wooden eggs are hidden throughout the Rural Park. Participants search for these treasures by solving riddles and following clues. The wooden eggs are then exchanged for real chocolate eggs.

troc.imageAlt: Troc’Jardin at Les Jardins de Wesserling
troc.title: Troc’Jardin
troc.subtitle: The last Sunday of April from 10am to 6pm. In the courtyard of the Wesserling Farm. Free entry.
troc.firstParagraph: Swap area. Fun workshops. Advice stands. Vegetable sales stand.
troc.secondParagraph: Refreshments, tarte flambée, plain or gratinated pretzels, crêpes.
troc.thirdParagraph: This is a special moment for amateur gardeners to exchange seedlings, tools and advice. Participants can drop off their items from 10am onwards. They are “paid” in the event’s special currency: radish coins, which can then be used to obtain plants and items of their choice. Radish coins can also be earned by taking part in games, buying a tarte flambée or purchasing an association membership card.

festival.imageAlt: Festival des Jardins Métissés at Les Jardins de Wesserling
festival.title: Festival des Jardins Métissés
festival.subtitle: From June to October. From 10am to 6.30pm.
festival.firstParagraph: Refreshments, tarts, salads, charcuterie or cheese platters, plain or gratinated pretzels, crêpes, ice creams.
festival.secondParagraph: The eco-museum of the Parc de Wesserling opens from May onwards. However, the Festival des Jardins Métissés begins in June. Each year, its temporary gardens built around a new theme transport visitors into poetic, artistic, playful and exotic worlds... perfect for wonderful family days out!

music.imageAlt: Fête de la Musique at Les Jardins de Wesserling
music.title: Fête de la Musique
music.subtitle: The Friday closest to 21 June. From 6pm to 11pm. In the courtyard of the Wesserling Farm. Free entry.
music.firstParagraph: Music throughout the evening. Free visit of the gardens and the Festival des Jardins Métissés.
music.secondParagraph: Refreshments, tarte flambée, plain or gratinated pretzels, crêpes, ice creams.
music.thirdParagraph: Music lovers can discover a variety of musical styles while seated beneath the farm shelters or on the slopes of the Rural Park. The Fête de la Musique at Wesserling takes place within the remarkable setting of Wesserling’s industrial heritage.

cocktail.imageAlt: Soirées cocktails at Les Jardins de Wesserling
cocktail.title: Soirées cocktails
cocktail.subtitle: Three Fridays in July. From 6pm to 10pm. In the Wesserling kitchen gardens. Paid entry through the gardens. One cocktail included with the entrance ticket.
cocktail.firstParagraph: Cocktails with or without alcohol, refreshments, tarte flambée, plain or gratinated pretzels, crêpes, ice creams.
cocktail.thirdParagraph: A moment of relaxation and conviviality in a garden that takes on a different appearance in the setting sun. A time to appreciate art in the garden in all its forms: musical, graphic, sculptural, choreographic and more.

nocturnes.imageAlt: Féeries Nocturnes at Les Jardins de Wesserling
nocturnes.title: Féeries Nocturnes

subtitle.text: Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays throughout August and during the week of 15 August. From 6.30pm to 11.30pm. Paid entry through the gardens.
subtitle.link: More information on the Parc de Wesserling website

nocturnes.firstParagraph: Large-scale game. Storytelling walks. Fire show.
nocturnes.secondParagraph: Refreshments, tarte flambée, plain or gratinated pretzels, crêpes, ice creams.
nocturnes.thirdParagraph: As night falls, the gardens light up and everything becomes magical. The Féeries Nocturnes are an unforgettable experience for families and friends alike.

automne.imageAlt: Fête d'Automne at Les Jardins de Wesserling
automne.title: Fête d'Automne
automne.subtitle: Sunday in mid-October. From 10am to 6.30pm. Paid entry through the Manufacturers’ Château.
automne.firstParagraph: Gardening advice. Apple juice pressing. Creative workshops. Vegetable sales stand.
automne.secondParagraph: Refreshments, tarte flambée, soup bar, plain or gratinated pretzels, crêpes, ice creams.
automne.thirdParagraph: Gardens glowing with autumn colours, abundant vegetable harvests... This is the final event before the end of the Festival of Mixed Gardens. Gardeners share their advice, visitors can watch apple juice being pressed and taste this seasonal product. A well-stocked soup bar highlights freshly harvested vegetables. Everything is designed to delight both the eyes and the taste buds.

christmas.imageAlt: Noël au jardin at Les Jardins de Wesserling
christmas.title: Noël au jardin

subtitle.text: Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays throughout December and during the week between Christmas and New Year. From 5pm to 11pm. Paid entry through the Manufacturers’ Château. Mulled wine or hot apple juice included with the entrance ticket.
subtitle.link: More information on the Parc de Wesserling website

christmas.firstParagraph: Theatrical walk through the illuminated gardens.
christmas.secondParagraph: Refreshments, mulled wine, hot apple juice, hot chocolate, warm open sandwiches, soups, desserts.
christmas.thirdParagraph: For around an hour, participants embark on a storytelling walk that leads them into the world of Christmas, its values and its magic, all within the illuminated gardens. The walk ends at the Wesserling Farm, decorated with warm Christmas displays, around a hot drink or a convivial meal.

meta.title: Our Association — Les Jardins de Wesserling
meta.description: Discover the Les Jardins de Wesserling association, its history, its social and environmental objectives, and its development since 2000.

intro.firstParagraph: The educational kitchen garden and the Resto du Potager are managed by the Les Jardins de Wesserling association, recognised as being of public interest. In 2025, the association has 240 individual or family members, representing around 800 people including family members.
intro.secondParagraph: Their motivation reflects the objectives of the association:

objectives.employment: Create employment opportunities, particularly for people experiencing difficulties in this area
objectives.heritage: Help showcase the remarkable industrial heritage of Wesserling
objectives.environment: Raise awareness about respect for the environment

intro.missionButton: More information about our social mission
intro.thirdParagraph: The association has been officially recognised as an Integration Worksite by the French State since 2004, benefiting from intermunicipal, departmental, regional, national and European funding.
intro.volunteersTitle: Volunteers also take part in many activities:

volunteerActions.gardenDesign: Design and development of the gardens
volunteerActions.governance: Participation in the management of the association

intro.closingParagraph: Volunteers play an essential role in the life and development of the association’s project.

history.title: History of the association
paragraphs: The Les Jardins de Wesserling association was created in 2000 by around thirty local residents to take on an ambitious challenge: creating employment through the redevelopment of the former industrial wasteland of the Parc de Wesserling.

It joined the federation of associations entrusted, first by the Haut-Rhin Department and later by the European Collectivity of Alsace, with overseeing the tourism redevelopment of this former centre of the textile industry in the Vosges Massif.

The gardens were designed by landscape architects Agnès Daval and Philippe Raguin with respect for the history of the site. Their layout was initially carried out thanks to the work of a volunteer surveyor, then developed over the years through the continued involvement of the association’s volunteers.

The early years relied mainly on collective commitment: clearing land, planting, market gardening, site management, selling produce, supporting people towards employment and organising activities. More than one hundred volunteers took part each year in the annual garden festival.

The association has always pursued the same objective: progressively professionalising activities whenever financial resources allowed it, in order to secure jobs and sustain the missions of the association’s project.

timelineItems.title: Creation of the association

actions.first: Creation of the association by around thirty local residents.
actions.second: Tourism redevelopment of the Wesserling industrial park.
actions.third: Creation of a decorative and educational kitchen garden open to the public.
actions.fourth: First festive event: Potager en Fête.

timelineItems.employees: Recruitment of 3 integration employees under the CES scheme.
timelineItems.volunteers: Volunteers handled management, employment support, land clearing, planting, harvesting, sales and activities.

timelineItems.title: Implementation of technical supervision

actions.first: Technical supervision introduced through the Emplois Jeunes scheme.
actions.second: State financial support for 5 years, provided the positions were made sustainable.

timelineItems.employees: Recruitment of 2 technical supervisors and 6 integration positions.
timelineItems.volunteers: Volunteers refocused on management, sales, employment support and activities.

timelineItems.title: Recognition as an Integration Workshop and Worksite

actions.first: Agreement with the State from 2004 onwards.
actions.second: Development of a winter activity: jams, syrups and quince paste.

timelineItems.employees: Technical supervisors’ positions made permanent. 10 integration positions, then CDDI contracts from 2008 onwards.
timelineItems.volunteers: Employees handled maintenance, production and processing. Volunteers developed educational installations, activities and management.

timelineItems.title: Professionalisation of management

actions.first: Professionalisation of administrative tasks and socio-professional support.
actions.second: Creation of shared positions with the Patrimoine et Emploi integration worksite.
actions.third: Support from a business management adviser through a DLA support scheme.

timelineItems.employees: Creation of 2 positions: one administrator and one socio-professional support officer.
timelineItems.volunteers: A member of the association voluntarily managed staff. Volunteers remained involved in design, development and management.

timelineItems.title: Development of activities

actions.second: Growing attractiveness of the educational kitchen garden.
actions.fourth: Creation of a light catering service in 2014/2017 with the support of a DLA scheme.

timelineItems.employees: At the end of 2018, creation of a shared management position with the PE integration worksite.
timelineItems.volunteers: Volunteer involvement remained strong, particularly in activities, which increased from 1 to 8 during the year.

timelineItems.title: Structuring and development of the team

actions.first: Separation of management, administration and socio-professional support positions.
actions.second: Conversion of positions to full-time roles.
actions.third: Creation of a market gardening sector.

timelineItems.employees: The association now employs around thirty staff members: 22 integration positions, one director, one administrator, one ASP officer and 3 technical supervisors.
timelineItems.volunteers: Volunteer involvement represents around 6,500 working hours every year.

meta.title: Social Mission — Les Jardins de Wesserling
meta.description: Discover the social mission of Les Jardins de Wesserling, its integration worksite and the support provided to employees in professional integration.

insertionWorksite.imageAlt: The integration worksite of Les Jardins de Wesserling
insertionWorksite.title: The integration worksite
insertionWorksite.firstParagraphStart: The Les Jardins de Wesserling association has been approved as an
insertionWorksite.firstParagraphEnd: by the French State since 2004. This scheme enables the association to receive financial compensation for employing and supporting people who have difficulty accessing employment: young people without training, unemployed people over 50, disabled people or people facing various temporary difficulties, ...
insertionWorksite.secondParagraphStart: The association is therefore part of the wider family of organisations for
insertionWorksite.secondParagraphEnd: , which represents 12 million jobs, supported by 11 million volunteers including 5 million regular volunteers.

employees.title: Employees of the integration worksite
employees.firstParagraph: The Les Jardins de Wesserling integration worksite currently offers 20 positions for employees in professional integration. 6 permanent employees support them on a daily basis: 3 technical supervisors, a socio-professional support worker, an administrative manager, a director, and 2 seasonal workers.
employees.secondParagraph: The work carried out through the integration worksite is based on gardening in the educational kitchen garden and in the market garden field, creating installations, service at the Resto du Potager, processing produce into jams, syrups, quince pastes and pickles, sales, and participation in events. Professional equipment is made available to them so that they can gain experience in different trades.
employees.thirdParagraph: Through multiple individual interviews and group discussions, employees in professional integration are supported in developing their project, undertaking qualifying training, carrying out work placements in companies (Periods of Professional Immersion during which the trainee remains employed by the integration worksite), removing barriers to employment, and applying for job offers.

application.title: Applying for a professional integration position
application.introduction: To apply for a professional integration position in an integration worksite, prior registration with France Travail and its approval are required. These positions are particularly reserved for:

eligibility.longTermUnemployed: Long-term unemployed people (more than one year)
eligibility.youngAndSenior: Young people under 26 and people over 50
eligibility.rsaRecipients: Recipients of RSA or people at the end of their unemployment benefit entitlement
eligibility.newcomers: People who have recently arrived in France

application.applicationProcess: Candidates submit their cover letter and curriculum vitae to the Les Jardins de Wesserling association, then attend a pre-employment interview, as in any company.
application.franceTravailInfo: Jobseekers may be invited by France Travail to meetings with all providers of Integration through Economic Activity, and in this way get to know future employers.

fse.title: The European Social Fund ESF
fse.firstParagraph: The European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) provides financial support to the Les Jardins de Wesserling integration worksite, particularly for recruitment, socio-professional support and the technical supervision of employees in professional integration.
fse.secondParagraph: The ESF+ is the European Union’s main instrument for supporting employment, training, social inclusion and the fight against poverty. The current funding period covers 2021–2027.
fse.thirdParagraph: The ESF+ is part of the European Union’s programming period 2021–2027. France has a budget of 6.7 billion euros for the ESF+ during this period. These credits are distributed between 2 national programs managed by the State and 17 regional programs:
fse.firstListItemStart: The General Delegation for Employment and Vocational Training (DGEFP) manages the
fse.nationalProgrammeLinkLabel: national ESF+ programme “employment, inclusion, youth and skills”
fse.firstListItemEnd: , with a budget of 4 billion euros for the 2021–2027 period.
fse.secondListItemStart: The General Directorate for Social Cohesion (DGCS) manages the
fse.foodAidProgrammeLinkLabel: national ESF+ programme “European support for food aid”
fse.secondListItemEnd: with a budget of 582 million euros for the 2021–2027 period.
fse.thirdListItemStart: The Regions (or the single territorial authorities in Corsica, French Guiana and Martinique) are the managing authorities for regional ERDF-ESF+ programmes, whose ESF+ components represent €2.1 billion.
fse.fourthParagraph: To ensure that actions are not funded twice by the ESF+, 'demarcation lines' agreed between the French State and Régions de France define the main principles for allocating responsibilities between the national ESF+ programme managed by the DGEFP and the 17 regional programmes, based on the legal responsibilities of each managing authority:
fse.firstListItem: The following areas of action fall under the national ESF+ programme 'Employment, Inclusion, Youth and Skills': the social and professional integration of people furthest from employment (except in the single territorial authorities), supporting young people towards employment and apprenticeships, developing employees' skills, quality of working life and professional equality;
fse.secondListItem: The following areas of action fall under the regional programmes: training for jobseekers, support for business creation, support for the social and solidarity economy, and lifelong career guidance (except in Mayotte and Saint Martin);
fse.thirdListItem: The allocation of responsibilities for certain issues, such as tackling early school leaving, is determined through local demarcation agreements.

textileParkAssociation.title: The Textile Park of Wesserling Management and Activities Association
textileParkAssociation.firstParagraph: The Parc de Wesserling, within which the Les Jardins de Wesserling association operates, is partly owned by the Haut-Rhin Department, now the European Collectivity of Alsace, and partly owned by the Community of Municipalities of the Saint-Amarin Valley.
textileParkAssociation.secondParagraph: The Haut-Rhin Department (now the CEA) delegated to the Textile Park of Wesserling Management and Activities Association the mission of converting this former textile industrial site into a tourist destination and managing it. It is a federation of associations, of which the Les Jardins de Wesserling association is a member. An agreement defines the terms of collaboration on the spaces shared by the two organisations.
textileParkAssociation.thirdParagraph: The Les Jardins de Wesserling association shares premises with the Wesserling Park Management Association and the Patrimoine et Emploi integration worksite. These premises were renovated and then made available to the organisations free of charge.

otherAssociations.title: Other partner associations
otherAssociations.paragraph: Various associations take part in the activities organised by the Les Jardins de Wesserling association: the Wesserling media library l’Etoffe des Mots, the Family Gardens of Thann, poultry and beekeeping associations, the SM4, the Ecojardiniers Na’Thur Doller, the Krempel & Pric a Prac recycling centre, Les Oiseaux du Stockenberg, the CPIE des Hautes Vosges, the LPO, the Moulin de Storckensohn, ...

membership.title: Join the association
membership.firstParagraph: Joining the association or becoming a donor provides a 66% tax benefit, as the association is recognised as being of public interest. This contributes to funding actions supporting employment.
membership.secondParagraph: To join the Les Jardins de Wesserling association, complete the membership form and return it with payment by cheque to “Association Les Jardins de Wesserling 16 rue de Ranspach 68470 Husseren-Wesserling”.
membership.thirdParagraph: Payment can also be made by bank transfer or by visiting the association’s offices in person.
